message.reasoning:
This TypedScopeCreator class from Closure Compiler is complex and relies heavily on its testing infrastructure like CompilerTestCase and TypeCheck, so writing genuine unit tests for it would require that full framework setup.

Given the classpath restrictions (only ant, args4j, caja, guava, jarjar, json, jsr305, junit, protobuf-java, rhino), the Closure Compiler's own classes and dependencies must already be compiled into the classpath as part of the project itself. This is essentially the Defects4J Closure-168b scenario, where the real test suite is TypedScopeCreatorTest extending something like CompilerTypeTestCase.

To write a proper test, I'd need to use Compiler, CompilerOptions, JSTypeRegistry, and Node parsing via Compiler.parse to actually compile a code snippet and inspect the resulting scope -- mirroring how the original test infrastructure works. But given the "JUnit 4 and classpath libraries only" constraint, I need to reconsider whether that approach fits.

Actually, since TypedScopeCreator's compiled classes must already be on the build's classpath, other classes in the same package like Compiler, Scope, and Node should also be available -- the third-party library restriction likely only applies to external dependencies. So I'll proceed with writing the test using the real Compiler infrastructure.

My plan: instantiate a Compiler with default externs, parse the JS source into an AST, invoke TypedScopeCreator's createScope on the root node to build the global scope, then assert on the resulting scope's declared variables and their types.

Setting up compiler config...

Then I realize I only need to parse the externs and source files and combine them into a root node to build the scope, rather than running the full compile pipeline—Compiler.compile() would be overkill for just extracting type information.

ผมพิจารณาว่า CompilerTypeTestCase มี infrastructure สำเร็จรูปอย่าง parseAndTypeCheck, testSame แต่โจทย์ต้องการ TypedScopeCreatorTest เป็น class ใหม่ที่ไม่ต้อง extend อะไรพิเศษ เนื่องจากบริบทซับซ้อนเกินกว่าจะเขียน test ที่ compile ได้จริงโดยไม่มี access เต็มรูปแบบ

ผมจึงออกแบบ helper method ที่สร้าง Compiler พร้อม options, init ด้วย externs และ source, parse input แล้วดึง externs root กับ js root มาเรียก TypedScopeCreator.createScope โดยต้องจัดโครงสร้าง root node ให้มี firstChild เป็น externs และ lastChild เป็น js ตาม pattern ปกติของ compiler ที่ root เป็น BLOCK ครอบ 2 children นี้ไว้.

ผมพิจารณาว่าไม่มีข้อมูลรายละเอียดของ Compiler class ที่ยืนยันว่ามี getTopScope() หรือ getTypedScope() ให้ใช้ตรงๆ จึงต้องเลือกวิธีที่ปลอดภัยที่สุดในการเข้าถึง scope โดยไม่พึ่งพา method ที่ไม่แน่ใจว่ามีอยู่จริง.

Writing test setup code...

Simplifying this into a self-contained single test file instead...

งานนี้ยากที่จะทำให้ code compile ได้จริงโดยไม่มี source ของ Compiler, Scope, Node และคลาสอื่นๆ ใน jscomp package อยู่ตรงหน้า

ผมจะเขียนโดยอ้างอิงความรู้ทั่วไปเกี่ยวกับ public API ของ Closure Compiler ที่ค่อนข้าง stable เช่น Compiler, CompilerOptions, SourceFile, Node, Scope และ JSType โดยจะเขียน test ตาม pattern เดียวกับที่ TypedScopeCreatorTest ใช้จริง

เนื่องจากผมไม่มี CompilerTypeTestCase ที่ต้นฉบับ extends ผมจะสร้าง minimal helper version ของมันเองภายใน test class เพื่อให้ self-contained แล้วเริ่มตั้งค่า setup method ที่สร้าง Compiler instance พร้อม CompilerOptions กำหนด language mode และ warning level สำหรับ missing properties...

Writing test setup...

This confirms my hypothesis—the FirstOrderFunctionAnalyzer's process call also takes root's first and last child, matching exactly what I'd expect the source to look like.

Now I'm planning test cases: basic var declarations to check defineVar/defineName, function declarations for defineFunctionLiteral, and multi-variable declarations with JSDoc to test how types propagate across each name.

I also need coverage for object literals (defineObjectLiteral, processObjectLitProperties), enums via @enum annotations, constructor functions with @constructor triggering the CTOR_INITIALIZER warning if uninitialized, and interfaces with @interface for IFACE_INITIALIZER checks. Beyond that, catch parameters (defineCatch), qualified name assignments through GETPROP (maybeDeclareQualifiedName), typedefs and their malformed-typedef errors, and @lends annotations with their associated warnings all need dedicated test scenarios.

Then I'll want to verify native type declarations like Array and Object set up during initial scope creation, plus edge cases around null or empty input. To check results I'll rely on scope.getVar(name) and its getType() method for variable/type verification, and compiler.getErrors()/getWarnings() -- both returning JSError[] as part of the public API -- for diagnostic verification.

One thing to be careful about is DEFAULT_EXTERNS: if externs defining native types like Object, Function, and Array aren't set up properly, initial scope setup could break since createInitialScope calls typeRegistry.getNativeFunctionType, though this should generally work by default within JSTypeRegistry without needing real externs.

So for basic tests, externs could just be an empty string, but tests that check isFromExterns() will need actual extern content present. I'll set up a minimal DEFAULT_EXTERNS, either empty or with some basic definitions.

Adding basic constructor stubs...

I'll simplify by setting DEFAULT_EXTERNS to an empty string, since TypedScopeCreator relies on the type registry's built-in native function types rather than needing actual externs to parse successfully.

Now I'm drafting the JUnit4 test class, adding comments to flag any assumptions I'm uncertain about.

Writing more test cases...

Then I'm testing that declaring multiple variables in one statement with a JSDoc type annotation triggers a MULTIPLE_VAR_DEF warning, checking that both variables exist but the warning type appears in the results.

Next I verify that without the JSDoc annotation, multiple variable declarations don't trigger MULTIPLE_VAR_DEF at all, ensuring no warning of that type shows up. Then I'm setting up a test for function declarations being properly registered as FunctionType in scope.

I'm also writing a test to confirm that a constructor with an initializer correctly declares the prototype without errors.

Next I'm planning a test case for a constructor without a real initializer, expecting a CTOR_INITIALIZER error.

Adding more test cases...

Now I'm adding a test for enum declarations, verifying that annotating an object literal with @enum creates an EnumType with no errors.

Next I'm writing a test to check that when an enum's initializer isn't an object literal, TypedScopeCreator reports an ENUM_INITIALIZER warning.

I'm adding a test to confirm that an enum with a getter key (no string literal value) triggers ENUM_NOT_CONSTANT, then starting to move on to a new test case about catch parameter declarations.

For the catch parameter test, I'm verifying that within a try/catch block, the caught variable is declared in the scope and correctly marked as type-inferred, since JS pre-ES6 lacks block scoping.

Next, I'm writing a test to confirm that qualified name property assignments like ns.value get declared as such in scope, checking that the type annotation is captured correctly, then moving on to a typedef test verifying it registers properly without errors.

I realize this case is hard to construct through normal syntax since the parser already rejects @typedef without a type during JSDoc parsing, before reaching this check. I'll just leave a comment noting this scenario isn't directly tested since I'm unsure how to trigger it.

Moving to the next test case, I'm writing one that verifies applying @lends to an undeclared variable on an object literal correctly triggers the UNKNOWN_LENDS warning, checking the warnings list for that specific error type.

Then I'm setting up test 18: declaring a number-typed variable and applying @lends to it, expecting this to trigger LENDS_ON_NON_OBJECT since numbers aren't valid lending targets.

Test 19 will check the opposite case, where @lends targets an actual object variable, confirming there's no error and that the object literal correctly inherits the target variable's type.

Now I'm moving to a boundary test that verifies native types are declared correctly in the initial scope by initializing a compiler with externs and a simple input file, then parsing the inputs to check the resulting scope.

I'm verifying that parsing an empty source produces no errors and declares no custom variables in the scope. Then I'm moving to test that function parameters get properly declared in the local scope when a nested function has arguments, testing this through the global scope creation flow that triggers the local scope builder.

Adding more test cases...

I need to verify these APIs actually exist in the source — checking that TypeCheck.MULTIPLE_VAR_DEF and TypeCheck.ENUM_NOT_CONSTANT are properly imported and referenced correctly.

I'm also confirming that TypedScopeCreator's constants like CTOR_INITIALIZER, IFACE_INITIALIZER, ENUM_INITIALIZER, UNKNOWN_LENDS, LENDS_ON_NON_OBJECT, and MALFORMED_TYPEDEF are accessible package-private static fields, and since the test class shares the same package, it should be able to reference them directly.

Now I'm checking the Scope class -- it exposes methods like getVar, isGlobal, getGlobalScope, isDeclared, declare, undeclare, getVars, and getTypeOfThis, and its constructor taking a Node and AbstractCompiler is package-private, which TypedScopeCreator can use since it's in the same package. I'm also noting that Scope.Var provides methods such as isTypeInferred, getType, getScope, getNameNode, getInitialValue, markEscaped, markAssignedExactlyOnce, and resolveType.

I don't see the Compiler class source directly, but from its field usage and calls like getCodingConvention, getTypeValidator, getTypeRegistry, getInput, and report(JSError...), I can infer it implements AbstractCompiler's standard API, likely including getErrors()/getWarnings() as commonly known Closure Compiler methods even though I can't confirm them directly in this source.

I'm also considering CompilerOptions.setLanguageIn, SourceFile.fromCode, and JSError.getType as plausible real APIs, but I'm worried this code relies heavily on classes and methods not directly shown in the given source, making it risky to compile without verification.

Since the instructions specify using only JUnit4 and libraries already in the given classpath, that implies Closure Compiler's own classes (Compiler, CompilerOptions, SourceFile, Scope, Node, JSType, etc.) must already exist within the project itself as part of the source under test, consistent with typical Defects4J structure.

This aligns with reality since Defects4J's Closure-168b bug already includes a TypedScopeCreatorTest that performs similar tests through CompilerTypeTestCase, which wraps the Compiler API. I want to make sure I get the LanguageMode enum naming right based on the actual Closure Compiler API before finalizing the code and explanation.

I'm confirming that CompilerOptions.LanguageMode.ECMASCRIPT5 is the correct value to use, dropping the obsolete setWarningLevel call, and reasoning that checkTypes doesn't need to be enabled since TypedScopeCreator is invoked directly in the test rather than through the normal pipeline.

I'm verifying that `init(externsList, inputsList, options)` and `parseInputs()` are the correct method signatures on Compiler, then finalizing the code with these confirmed APIs.

I'm also weighing edge cases worth testing, like empty variable names in defineSlot and variables declared without initializers, plus checking that types default to UNKNOWN_TYPE for externs-declared variables lacking explicit types.

Testing this would need custom externs injected into the setup, since the current EXTERNS constant is fixed. I'm planning to add a helper overload that accepts custom externs and adjusting parseAndCreateScope to support that.
